interest: Rare U.S. account of prewar Tokyo policing and Japanese protests against police torture.
overview: This State Department decimal file (894.105) documents U.S. diplomatic reporting on the organization, administrative structure, and coercive methods of the Japanese police between June 1933 and December 1936. The centerpiece of the file is a comprehensive fifteen-page Embassy report compiled in January 1936 detailing the centralized hierarchy of the Japanese police system under the Ministry of Home Affairs, ranks and judicial summary powers, training schools, fire brigades, and the extensive bureau-by-bureau breakdown of the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Board (including the Special Higher Police, or Tokko). The latter half of the file, from late 1936, contains despatches and Japanese press clippings reporting on widespread police brutality and torture scandals, notably the indictment of police officers in Kanagawa Prefecture for torturing election law suspects, public protests led by bar associations, mistreatment of foreign tourists and consular staff, and the political friction between bureaucratic-police power and civil liberties under constitutional government.

subfiles.about: Comprehensive report detailing the centralization, legal powers, personnel statistics, training schools, and institutional structure of the Japanese police and the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Board.
subfiles.from: Charles E. Cooper, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: This fifteen-page report examines the centralized administration of the Japanese police under the Minister of Home Affairs, noting that local authorities exercise virtually no independent control over police affairs. It details police ranks (chokunin, sonin, hansin), minor judicial summary jurisdiction, armaments, and nationwide statistics as of 1933 encompassing over 65,000 personnel. The report describes police and fire-brigade training institutions, including the Higher Police Training School in Tokyo and prefectural schools. Pages 10 through 18 provide a structural diagram and detailed functional descriptions of the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Board's Secretariat and its six departments: Police Affairs, Special Higher Service (Tokko), Detective, Peace Preservation, Health and Sanitation, and Fire.
subfiles.title: Report on the Police Organization of Japan (Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 1657)
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
